_readme: The scorer config score_functions.py --config reads. Copy it to
security-review/scorers.json (or anywhere) and edit; nothing reads this
file by default, so the example can name an endpoint that does not exist.
`backend` picks the default; --backend overrides it. `backends.<name>` is
handed to that backend and to no other, so three configurations can live
here and only the selected one is read.
THE THREE THINGS TO GET RIGHT IN `finetuned`, in order of how quietly they
fail:
context_profile  must name the profile extract_functions.py --context-profile
was run with. A model fed a window it was not trained on
still returns a number; the number is just not calibrated.
score_functions.py compares this against the corpus and
downgrades the run to an ordering when they differ
(downgrade code context_profile_mismatch).
verdict_tokens   the exact token strings the model was trained to emit. A
near miss does not error - the endpoint answers, the
tokens are absent from the top-k, and every score comes
from the bounded fallback. scorer-report.json counts
those, and a run where the count equals the corpus size
has the wrong tokens configured.
evalset_id       the bare id (a name, never a path) of a file under
assets/evalsets/ frozen BEFORE the ledger started
producing samples, whose kind is "calibration" and which
records a measured base_rate and at least one measured
operating point. A population such as
baseline-2026-09 fixes a population and is refused. It is
the only thing that lets this backend keep
score_kind: "probability"; see assets/evalsets/README.md.
Numeric settings (batch_size, timeout, max_retries, retry_backoff_seconds,
logprobs) take their default when absent and are refused when present and
out of range; max_retries: 0 disables retries. A redirect from the endpoint
is refused rather than followed, so `endpoint` must be the final URL.
`backends.rules.weights` overrides any of the WEIGHTS in
tools/scorers/rules_backend.py, and scorer-report.json prints the weights a
run applied. repeat_decay 0, rule_weight_cap 12 and sample_tree_penalty 0
together reproduce rules@1.0.0; a config copied from an older example that
still says rule_weight_cap 12 keeps the old cap.
`operating_point` is optional. The config chooses the mode, the flags
(--strict-k, --loose-percent, --budget) choose the size: a `k` or `percent`
written here is used only when the flag is not given, and a size flag for a
tier this config puts in another mode is refused. mode "score" is
accepted ONLY when the run really carries a calibrated probability - over an
ordinal score it is a hard error, not a downgrade, and there is no flag that
relaxes it. See pipeline-contract.md §6.
